fronts.text:
P1 ↓

Seven policy families cover transport, startup, shutdown, delivery, output, resources and diagnostics. Values are derived once, frozen and exactly validated across hops; no user flags/environment/config tune them. Serialization/override factories end package-internal; AST, declaration, runtime, manifest and dependency checks enforce that surface.

STATED Architecture and policy plans require one complete snapshot and no user tuning. #130 stages snapshot transport and enforceable ownership; #131 adopts it. Temporary public bridges retire later. Source ↗

P2 ↓

Status gets 100 ms, ordinary lifecycle 250 ms, admission 5 s. Accepted completion, healthy warm-up, startup silence, worker-output acknowledgement and unacknowledged result retention have no corresponding deadline/eviction here. Silence, retention and idle-accounting changes are deferred.

STATED The policy record names these distinct purposes and intentional absences; follow-up specs retain the deferred work. Source ↗

P3 ↓

Resource limits derive from effective constrained/total memory with clamps and hysteresis. Output has chunk/inline/per-result/aggregate bounds; diagnostics and replacements have independent retention/capacity limits. The deeper numeric table is the same seven-family policy.

STATED The policy record supplies a reason per threshold/recipe; these reasons explain purpose and preservation, not empirical proof that each exact number is optimal. Source ↗

P4 ↓

Worker wrapper deserializes the complete policy before new Worker. A malformed injected snapshot can now throw in the parent constructor before a worker or its startup handlers exist.

UNEXPLAINED This source-order consequence accompanies #131 chunk-limit adoption. No separate reason for moving this malformed-input failure boundary was found. Source ↗

P5 ↓

Admission order is authentication, readiness, resource pause, queue, then duplicate compatibility. Compatibility reads do not mutate the ledger. Authentication disconnects; not-ready/draining/resource-pressure are retry-safe, incompatible is not. Contradictory code/boolean frames are corrupt. The staging request field stays unknown to avoid a CLI type dependency.

STATED PR #134 centralizes first-failure order and code-derived retry safety while preserving dependency direction. Source ↗

P6 ↓

Outer failure precedence is resource interruption → result capacity → worker exit (or stopping) → shutdown code → stopping/internal. Worker failures use a separate four-word vocabulary; concrete instanceof facts stay with mechanism owners.

STATED PR #133 separates domains and makes classification pure while preserving subtype behavior. Source ↗

P7 ↓

Test adapters can change the stimulus: inline zero may become a positive floor (transport: at least one 64-KiB chunk); a legacy memoryCapBytes option is accepted but not forwarded. Empty-directory assertions may therefore observe an empty directory without a spill.

UNEXPLAINED Test-only tuning is stated in #131. The exact compatibility floors and ignored option are not separately justified in the supplied record. Source ↗

P8 ↓

Spool fixtures now coordinate chunk/inline/result limits and enlarge payloads; a capture threshold changes 1→32. The benchmark resource-policy object gains replacement window/limit fields while schemaVersion remains 1. These are test/reporting decisions, alongside production policy.

UNEXPLAINED No separate rationale for every changed fixture threshold or unversioned benchmark field was located. Source ↗

P9 ↓

Accepted execute reattachment and result-fetch resume use independent numeric counters. Factory defaults are one reattachment and one fetch per execute attempt; a reattached attempt gets a fresh inner allowance. Neither counter authorizes local replay of accepted work.

STATED PR #131 explains the two scopes; #142 gives their final execution-client owner. Episode 06 works through the retained identity and fresh capture. Source ↗

R1 ↓

One receiver retains manifest identity, digest progress and the next RECORD offset across fetch connections; each connection gets a fresh decoder. Offset advances after awaited append, never on receipt alone.

STATED PR #138 gives durable capture and wire framing different lifetimes. Source ↗

R2 ↓

A reattached execute attempt allocates fresh output and a fresh per-attempt fetch allowance. Both counters are numeric and independent (factory defaults: one fetch and one reattachment). Only eligible authenticated accepted closure can trigger reattachment.

STATED PRs #131 and #142 explicitly separate the two recovery scopes. Source ↗

R3 ↓

At the tip, repeated eligible fetch closures can consume the configured allowance; exhausted fetch-ended becomes accepted corruption. Accepted-close reattachment exhaustion preserves the original accepted-close error. This supersedes the intermediate #131 later-completion-error behavior.

STATED PR #142 says exhaustion retains accepted-corruption behavior; its implementation stores originalAcceptedClose. This page describes the final delta, not #131 as the final transport. Source ↗

R4 ↓

Manifest/end coordinates, record count, byte count and digest must agree. Failed capture is disposed; successful finish transfers disposal to the caller for replay/ack cleanup. ACK uses a narrow completion-only lifecycle-client capability. Warm capture/storage and controlled failure outputs belong to daemon.

STATED PRs #138, #142 and #148 specify capture ownership, transfer cleanup and the narrow ACK capability. Source ↗

R5 ↓

Before accepted completion, only retry-safe transport failure can fall back locally. Once receipt is accepted, completion failure returns controlled warm failure output, not a second local execution.

STATED The architecture and #148 keep route, output and replay-safety decisions inside the client. Source ↗
